name: barbed devil
damage_resistances: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical weapons that aren't silvered

special_abilities.name: barbed hide
special_abilities.desc: At the start of each of its turns, the barbed devil deals 5 (1d10) piercing damage to any creature grappling it.

special_abilities.name: devil's sight
special_abilities.desc: Magical darkness doesn't impede the devil's darkvision.

special_abilities.name: magic resistance
special_abilities.desc: The devil has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: multiattack
actions.desc: The devil makes three melee attacks: one with its tail and two with its claws. Alternatively, it can use Hurl Flame twice.

actions.name: claw
actions.desc: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage.

actions.name: tail
actions.desc: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) piercing damage.

actions.name: hurl flame
actions.desc: Ranged Spell Attack: +5 to hit, range 150 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (3d6) fire damage. If the target is a flammable object that isn't being worn or carried, it also catches fire.

lore:
The Hamatula, or Barbed Devil, is a nightmare of serrated obsidian and malice. Native to the jagged, iron-streaked wastes of the Nine Hells, these creatures are rarely seen in our world unless bound by the desperate rites of a foolhardy warlock. They haunt desolate ruins and lightless vaults, serving as eternal, unblinking sentinels.

Their predation is a gruesome art. Unlike the swift strike of a wolf, the Hamatula favors a slow, agonizing embrace. It lunges with elongated limbs, pulling the victim flush against a torso bristling with razor-sharp spines. Once snagged, there is no escape; the barbs are hooked, designed to tear deeper with every struggle. They do not merely kill; they "harvest" the fear of the trapped.

In the folklore of the Lowlands, they are whispered of as "The Thistle-Men." Peasants claim a Barbed Devil is born from every oath broken in greed—a manifestation of the stinging consequences of betrayal. To see one’s shadow sprout thorns is a death sentence, a sign that the infernal tithe is due. Do not seek mercy from the briar, traveler; it knows only the cold hunger of the hook.
